rationale: ⚠️ The typed media update rejects an unknown-field body with a JSON-processing 400. Its response contract lists only 200; documenting the rejection explains this status discrepancy.

⚠️ A link-deserialization failure is mapped by the catch-all exception handler to 500. Malformed client input should receive a controlled client error; the response identifies parsing, not infrastructure failure.
⚠️ Cart clearing identifies the customer through Principal and takes no name query argument. The successful parameter-free request matches that design; the specification incorrectly requires name.

⚠️ attrs is documented in source as a comma-separated attribute list. A one-character ceiling cannot represent ordinary field names; accepting the longer filter exposes an overly restrictive specification.
⚠️ The empty category reaches persistence without required-field validation. The correlated log records a NULL GRP constraint failure, explaining the 500 as missing implementation validation.

⚠️ The schema permits omitting name, while the handler explicitly requires it and returns 400. The supplied evidence does not establish whether an empty update should succeed or the contract should require name.

⚠️ The group parameter performs substring filtering on category groups, with no one-character restriction in source. The specification ceiling conflicts with that search behavior and the accepted longer value.

⚠️ The update-specific schema requires status, but the shared Pet schema requires only name and photoUrls. Source permits a nullable status; the successful update supports an erroneous extra requirement.
⚠️ Updating nonexistent id 0 dereferences the missing persisted message. The correlated stack points to setValue without a null check, so the 500 comes from implementation error handling.

⚠️ Source explicitly declares GET for reading media metadata. The specification places the matching read operation under POST, so the undocumented-operation finding reflects a method error in the specification.

⚠️ Adding a cart item is explicitly mapped to PUT in source, while the specification substitutes PATCH. That explains the operation finding; the observed parsing 500 is an additional implementation problem.
⚠️ The response schema requires status although the shared Pet model does not. The form overload returns the created pet with absent optional status, exposing an overly strict response contract.
⚠️ The empty category is persisted without validating its non-null group. The matching log confirms a database NULL GRP violation; this server failure is caused by missing input validation.
⚠️ The inline category schema limits names to one character despite its own Dogs example. Source seeds Dogs and accepts ordinary category strings; the ceiling is a specification defect.
⚠️ Source intentionally adds a Shopping cart relation. The response contract instead closes _links around an empty boolean property, excluding the very relation the endpoint constructs.

⚠️ Source declares the download as GET, but the specification lists POST. This method mismatch explains the operation finding, independently of the missing-media null dereference causing the recorded 500.
⚠️ The source maps ping to GET and deliberately returns no content. The observed 204 matches it; the specification incorrectly assigns this operation to POST.
⚠️ Source explicitly rejects an empty card number and maps validation errors to 406. The empty-body-field response follows that path, but the specification omits the validation response.
⚠️ Order listing uses the authenticated Principal and accepts no name query argument. The request correctly succeeds without name; the required query declaration is erroneous.

⚠️ The controller does not consume a name query parameter when clearing the cart. Applying a one-character constraint to that unused parameter is a specification error, not a missing business validation.

⚠️ An overflowing order identifier raises a conversion exception that the catch-all handler maps to 500. Input conversion needs controlled client-error handling, rather than an internal-server-error response.
⚠️ The request and shared User model allow absent lastName. Source returns the created object with nullable fields; requiring lastName in every response incorrectly strengthens that model.

⚠️ The recorded GET returns the inventory map produced by getInventory. The specification assigns this read operation to POST; source behavior and retrieval semantics support correcting the specified method.
⚠️ time_max is a nullable Integer and null serialization is explicitly disabled. The empty activity revision legitimately omits it; the response schema incorrectly requires every nullable property.
⚠️ The update loads missing media id 0 and immediately calls a setter on null. The matching stack identifies that dereference, making the 500 an implementation defect.

⚠️ User lookup dereferences stored usernames without null checks, and earlier creation accepted a null username. This explains a plausible server-side failure path for the 500; logging does not establish its exact stack.

⚠️ participants_min is nullable in the activity model, and serialization explicitly omits nulls. Creation from an empty properties object therefore omits it; the mandatory response declaration is overly strict.

⚠️ The schema allows unknown properties, but a body containing only unknown keys receives a JSON-processing 400. The package does not establish whether extensible input or strict typed binding is intended.

⚠️ Source explicitly maps TAN generation to POST and documents 400 for a nonexistent registration token. The specification incorrectly places the operation under GET, causing the undocumented-operation finding.
⚠️ The controller explicitly exposes cart viewing through GET. The specification replaces that operation with POST; the successful recorded GET follows the source mapping.

⚠️ The product controller deliberately attaches links through RepresentationModel. The observed JSON serializes them as links, while the closed response schema permits only _links; the documented representation is inaccurate.

⚠️ The schema permits an empty array, while the handler explicitly rejects one. No additional evidence decides whether empty creation should be a successful no-op or a documented minimum-size violation.

⚠️ The POST reaches upload handling and returns its missing-pet response. The specification lists GET for this state-changing upload, so a specified-method error best explains the operation discrepancy.

⚠️ The reported finding is unsupported form decoding in the checker. The specification advertises this encoding and source supplies a form overload; the accompanying 500 is a separate unresolved server failure.

⚠️ Form creation overwrites the initialized photoUrls list with null and stores the pet unchecked. The earlier write and later listing contain the same id without required photoUrls, showing a persistence-validation defect.

⚠️ shipDate is optional in the shared Order request model and nullable in source. The controller returns the submitted order; requiring an omitted date in the response is an inconsistent specification constraint.

⚠️ The request supplies a syntactically valid placeholder token without creating its session. Source checks session existence and intentionally returns documented 400, so schema validity alone does not justify expecting success.
⚠️ The count filter is a nullable Long and is applied only when present. Listing categories without it is intentional; the specification incorrectly requires this optional filter.

⚠️ The recorded GET executes the source tag-search behavior and returns an empty result. The specification assigns this retrieval operation to POST, making the specified HTTP method the likely defect.
⚠️ The huge identifier cannot convert to Java long. A broad exception handler translates that client input error into 500; the correlated log confirms conversion rather than a downstream outage.

⚠️ Earlier creation stores a user without username. Lookup then calls equals on that null username before returning not-found, explaining why an unknown user produces 500 instead of the documented 404.
⚠️ Login returns a session unconditionally and never checks its username or password arguments. Accepting a request missing required login credentials is missing implementation validation.
⚠️ Source explicitly maps delivery changes to PUT with an included query parameter. The successful request matches it, while the specification lists PATCH instead.
⚠️ Source requires the missing registration fields and explicitly maps their validation failures to 406. The specification omits this intentional validation response, causing the status discrepancy.

⚠️ Source attaches product hyperlinks and the observed representation uses a links array. The response schema instead mandates _links, so its required property describes the wrong serialized representation.
⚠️ Invalid TAN verification raises 404 and the exception handler deliberately builds an empty response. The specification incorrectly promises an object body for that response.

⚠️ Registration requires key and keyType through explicit NotNull constraints. Their absence is correctly rejected; the specification omits the corresponding required declarations and wrongly validates the empty object.

⚠️ emailAddress is nullable in source and null serialization is explicitly suppressed. Creating a user without email therefore omits email_address; the response schema incorrectly makes that field mandatory.

⚠️ The response identifies a client link-deserialization failure. The generic exception handler maps that parse exception to 500 instead of a controlled client error, revealing an implementation error-handling defect.

⚠️ The finding reports unsupported header serialization in the checker. The recorded Authorization-bearing call succeeds with 201, and source accepts a wrapper token; checker limitations prevent assessing the advertised parameter shape.
